headline: A collaborative AI laboratory reports a theory-led diamond-spin experiment
summary: A preprint reports a collaborative LLM-agent laboratory that derived and tested a calibration law for ensembles of nitrogen-vacancy spins in diamond. The agents rejected an initial experiment design because ordinary interpolation could make the same predictions, then rejected an acquisition that met its accuracy criteria because phase and reference controls failed during signal drift. Authors report that the agents revised the protocol without relaxing precommitted criteria; a six-hour randomized acquisition then passed the stated controls and supported predictions on four withheld pulse sequences. These are author-reported results from one laboratory study. The data and analysis are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request; they were not independently inspected or reproduced here.
